15_marg1219: OCHOZIAS FELL. The house of Ochozias is the synagogue, which was surrounded on every side by the legal precepts as by the lattice of an upper chamber. But as Ochozias, falling through the lattice by which he should have been protected, incurred a grievous sickness, so the Jew too, going beyond the safeguard of the law, fell into a desperate languor of sins; where, because he forsook the help of God, he did not find the remedy of salvation. For he fled, like the impious king, to false gods, and therefore he is rebuked by the prophetic mouth and his approaching death is foretold. Ochozias signifies above all the princes of the Jews, who, given to vices, persecute the truth. Whence: "The princes and Pharisees sent ministers to apprehend Jesus" etc.
15_interl1550: El in Syriac [is] 'sun'; with b added, 'bel'; hence, according to the variety of tongues, bel, bal, baal, beelzebub.
15_marg1220: The captain of fifty is the confession of penance, by which the remission of sins is declared. The Jews, then, unwilling that Christ be God or the prince of penance, say to him: "Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?" And in the future they are burnt with fire. The third captain of fifty, because, converted to the faith of the Trinity, he knew the sacrament of penance, deserved pardon.
15_interl1551: who, railing, said: Man of God, come down
15_marg1221: BY A WHIRLWIND. The whirlwind, that is, a most violent wind, caught Elias up into the aery heaven, whence the birds of heaven [are so called], that it might suddenly set him down in a certain secret region of the earth, where he might live now in great quiet of flesh and spirit until at the end of the world he pays the debt of death. The fiery chariot by which he is said to have been caught up is the angelic powers, by whose working he was lifted up.
15_marg1222: The taking up of Elias signifies the Lord's ascension. Elias went up in a chariot, because a mere man needed another's help. Our Redeemer [went up] not in a chariot, because he who had made all things was borne above all things by his own power. In designation of his ascension the Lord had forerunners and witnesses, one before the law, the other under the law, that at length he himself might come who would truly pierce the heavens; who would also bestow cleanness of flesh on believers, and under whom the virtue of chastity would grow through the increase of the times. For Henoch was translated, begetting and begotten through intercourse; Elias was caught up, only begotten through intercourse; the Lord was taken up neither begetting nor begotten through intercourse.
15_interl1555: Christ our head to the Church his body
15_marg1223: Elias was eminently strong in the prophetic spirit and the working of miracles. The twofold grace, then, which Eliseus knew to flourish in his master, he asked to be given to himself. Whence it is plain that he did not ask that the disciple be above the master.
15_marg1224: RABANUS. Having received from the Lord confidence to ask, the Church asks for the double spirit of Christ, both because she needs the remission of sins, which Christ did not need, and the gift of the virtues, which Christ bestows from his fulness through the Holy Spirit, who "ascending on high, led captivity captive; he gave gifts to men," namely to those who put their hope in him. Hence it is that he says: If thou see me when I am taken from thee, that is, if thou open the eyes of faith and believe faithfully my ascension also, with my passion and resurrection, thou shalt obtain the effect of thy petition.
15_marg1225: RABANUS. [The mantle] is the incarnation, through which he broke through the river of death and prepared for us the passage to life. This Eliseus kept after the passing of Elias, because the Church kept the faith of the incarnation after the ascension of Christ, through which she is busy to pass over the waves of the present life. But as Eliseus divided the waters only by calling on the name of Elias, so the Church can do no works of power except through calling on the name of Christ. For it is God who worketh in us both to will and to accomplish.
15_marg1226: PUT SALT INTO IT. ISIDORE. Salt, that is, wisdom, placed in an earthen vessel, that is, the human body, heals the waters, that is, makes the peoples fruitful with the sweetness of love and good works through the incarnation of Christ.
15_marg1227: ISIDORE. Eliseus, 'salvation of God'. He is the one called Saviour, whom the Jews mock, because he was to go up on the cross in the place of Calvary. But Christ, after he ascended into heaven, as Eliseus went up to Bethel, that is, to the house of God, in the forty-second year sent two bears from the woods of the gentiles, namely Vespasian and Titus, who cast them down with cruel slaughter. And their blood was shed there where [they shed that of] the Lord.
15_marg1228: THE KING OF ISRAEL, THE KING OF JUDA, THE KING OF EDOM. RABANUS. The three kings warring against Moab are the rulers of the faithful, who through faith in the Trinity contend with spiritual arms against the prince of the world and [his] people, that is, philosophers, heretics, schismatics and all the wicked. Moab is interpreted 'of the father'; it fits those to whom the Lord said: "You are of your father the devil." These oppose the Church with threats, persecutions and guile, but are put to flight through Christ, who is the head of Christians.
15_marg1229: MAKE THE CHANNEL. RABANUS. The prophet provides for the people wearied with thirst by a miracle, and the sayings of prophecy afford counsel to the faithful how they may refresh the mind with spiritual doctrine.
15_marg1230: RABANUS. He makes ditches in the channel of the torrent who seeks the deep mysteries in the Scriptures. These are filled with water without rain and wind, because divine power often confers wisdom on its searchers without human help. Whence John says: "You have no need that any man teach you; but as his unction teacheth you of all things." Whence men and beasts will drink, that is, the clever and the simple will receive doctrine.
15_marg1231: RABANUS. For it does not suffice the servants of God to know hidden mysteries; they ought also to preach them to others and refute the gainsayers; to whom sure victory over the enemy is promised, that they may smite every city.
15_marg1232: RABANUS. The city is worldly prudence, in which philosophers and heretics trust. This is overthrown by the preachers.
15_marg1233: RABANUS. Not that which bears fruit, but deadly [fruit], which, cut down at the coming examination, will become fuel for the eternal fire. The fountains of waters are stopped up when the heresiarchs with their followers are condemned by the catholics. 'The goodly fields are covered with stones' when the comeliness of heretical and philosophical speech is overwhelmed by the weight of anathema. Only 'the walls of clay' remain, that is, false reasonings, which are brought to nothing by the slingers, that is, the holy preachers.
15_marg1234: RABANUS. So the philosophers, thinking the word of the cross foolishness, mock the passion of Christ and think the martyrdom of the Church madness.
15_marg1235: A CERTAIN WOMAN. Holy Church is the mother of two peoples, that is, the Jewish and the gentile, who formerly, by consenting in perverse work to the persuasion of the crafty spirit, had received from a creditor as it were a certain coin of sin, and feared to lose the two sons whom she had begotten in faith. But obeying the words of the prophet, that is, the precepts of sacred Scripture, she poured out from the little oil she had into empty vessels; because while the empty minds of many draw a little of the love of the divinity from the mouth of one teacher, they are filled to the top by the overflowing grace of the ointments of divine love; and now the hearts of many, which before were empty vessels, are full of the ointment of the Spirit, which seemed to be poured only from a scant amount of oil. While this is given to others and others, and faith is received by the hearers, the woman, that is, holy Church, rescued, is no longer held under the debt of her creditor. The woman who received the prophet as guest suggests the origin of the Israelite people, which was in the patriarchs. Whence, as she received the prophet Eliseus as guest, so they too received the Lord of the prophets as guest. For Abraham and Sara received and fed three men.
15_interl1563: the Lord [said] like things to Abraham: at this time Sara shall have a son
15_marg1236: AND THE CHILD GREW. RABANUS. So the Israelite people, after it grew up in Egypt and, led out into the desert by Moses, had heard the voice of the Lord, when it ought to have been enlightened with the light of knowledge, soon, running back in mind to idolatry, died.
15_marg1237: THEN HE SAID TO GIEZI. RABANUS. When the Lord gave the law through Moses, he sent as it were a rod by a servant; but the servant could not raise the dead by the rod, that is, by the terror of the law, because "the law brought nothing to perfection." Coming himself in person, he stretches himself upon the body, because "being in the form of God, he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant." He walked to and fro, because he calls both Jews and gentiles to eternal things through faith. He breathes seven times upon the dead, because by opening the divine gift he breathes the grace of the sevenfold Spirit upon those lying in the death of sin. And soon the child whom the rod of terror could not raise returned to life through the spirit of love.
15_interl1566: not indeed of bread, but of hearing the word of God
15_marg1238: That is, of the preachers, who walk in the law of the Lord and search his testimonies, [and] live always in the presence of the Saviour.
15_interl1567: that is, wild gourds, smaller than those that grow in gardens, and very bitter
15_marg1239: He who, intent on the letter of the law, or studious of philosophy, taking bitterness from the law or what is deadly from the philosophers, mixes it with gospel truth and, cooking it in the pot of his heart, prepares such a pottage, that is, teaching, for his hearers. For the Apostle says: "The letter killeth." "The wisdom of the flesh is death; but the wisdom of the spirit is life." The faithful, knowing this, cry: death in the pot. But meal is put into the pot when spiritual knowledge is brought into such a seasoning, that, the bitterness being shut out, the food becomes wholesome.
15_marg1240: AND A CERTAIN MAN CAME FROM BAALSALISA. RABANUS. This man is the company of the fathers, who is from Baalsalisa because it keeps the number three in the confession of the Trinity; for Baalsalisa is interpreted 'having a third'. This man offers to the man of God loaves of the firstfruits when, inspired by his grace, he offers to the Redeemer the books composed on the origin of creatures. He offers new corn in his scrip when he brings forth the New Testament in the writings of the gospel and the apostles. Our Eliseus commands his ministers, that is, the preachers, to dispense these to the faithful and "bring forth out of their treasure new things and old." Which mystery we read in the gospel in the breaking of the five and the seven loaves, where, the crowds being filled, they gathered twelve baskets or seven hampers of fragments, because no one grasps the sacraments of Scripture in every respect, but something remains over after he is filled, according to the word of the Lord.
15_marg1241: [Naaman] signifies the gentiles, holding sovereignty by strength in war and enjoying the beauty of things. Whence Naaman is interpreted [unclear in the edition: "decus suus commotio eorum"]. A valiant man and rich but a leper, because, though he seemed to have dominion through the power of his kingdom and the abundance of his goods, yet he appeared foul with leprosy through the error of idolatry.
15_marg1242: RABANUS. The robbers went out from Syria, which is 'loftiness', when the gentiles, led by greed and entangled in various business, wandered through the whole earth. These led captive from the land of Israel the girl who testified of the prophet in Israel, because the fame of Israel, carried by the merchants of the gentiles through the whole world, made known to the curiosity of men, which the wife of Naaman signifies, that a true prophet and Saviour remained in Judea. Hearing this, Naaman told his lord, when those to whom knowledge of the word has come suggest to those over them the greatness of spiritual knowledge. The king of Syria sends letters to the king of Israel for the health of his servant, when the leaders of the gentiles, hearing that God is in Israel, providing for the health of their own, send an embassy into Judea, that it may receive faith in the Saviour through the apostolic doctrine. Whence Cornelius sends from Caesarea to Joppe to Peter. The king rent his garments, because the priests, scribes and Pharisees, the rulers of the Jews, seeing the peoples coming together from every side to redemption, thinking it as it were blasphemy, rent their garments, as the prince of the priests did in the gospel. Let him come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel; and the Lord, whom he foreknew, these he also called etc. The gentile people, coming to the house of Eliseus, namely holy Church, received through the messenger, that is, the gospel preachers, [the command] to wash himself seven times in the Jordan, "born again of water and the Spirit." The Jordan signifies baptism, because in it the Saviour consecrated baptism for us. Naaman, despising the washing in the Jordan, signifies the simplicity of the unlearned, who could not understand the spiritual efficacy, because "the sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God." The servants with better counsel persuaded him to the prophet's command, because the Lord often reveals to the lesser what is better, since "God is not a respecter of persons." Having washed seven times, his flesh was restored like a child's, because each one, cleansed in baptism through the invocation of the sevenfold Spirit, is brought back to the infancy of an innocent life. Because in baptism we are commanded to renounce Satan and confess the faith of the Lord, Naaman declares he will no more offer sacrifice to the gods, [but] will serve God alone in all things. He takes a portion of the holy land with him, because the baptized must be strengthened by participation in the Lord's body.
15_interl1568: This is the catholic profession, since "All the gods of the Gentiles are devils: but the Lord made the heavens"
15_marg1243: I BESEECH etc. OF THE EARTH. Naaman took a portion of the holy land with him, to place it in the temple of the idols and, standing upon it, to adore the Lord whose land it was, lest he offend his own lord if he did not adore with him.
15_marg1244: RABANUS. [Giezi] is interpreted 'seeing a precipice' or 'vision of the valley'. He is Israel, who was once the servant of God; whence: "Israel was a child, and I loved him." But after, spurning the gospel, he cast himself headlong into the pit of avarice, which the sons of God reborn through baptism spurned, by just judgment he brought on himself the leprosy of error which the believers had laid aside. So all who after baptism and amendment of life return to their former ways are wrapped again in the filth which they hoped they had put off: "This is the dog returned to his vomit."
15_marg1245: AND IT HAPPENED, AS ONE WAS FELLING SOME TIMBER. RABANUS. When the presence of Christ, working through the body, cut down the impious Jews as unfruitful trees. Whence: "Behold the axe is laid to the root of the trees." By them, the passion intervening, [the spirit] left the body itself [and] went down to the depths; which [body], laid in the tomb, rose again, the spirit returning as it were to the handle.
15_marg1246: RABANUS. Great care must be taken lest the understanding grow torpid in idleness, lest in the exercise of work it vanish through the vice of elation.
15_marg1247: Morally. The iron in the handle is the understanding in the heart. With this wood is cut when evildoers are rebuked; which, while it is done loosely, while the slip of vainglory is not avoided [the iron flies off]. The iron is lost in the water, because through slack work the understanding is made foolish, which is given for this, that it be restored before the eyes of the giver by good action. Whence it follows: This very thing I had borrowed. But the elect, if ever they offend, quickly return to the heart and pursue the fault with tears. Whence: Alas, alas, my lord. Weeping, they carefully look not only at the evils they have committed, but also at the good things they ought to have rendered from the gift received. And this is: Alas, alas, alas, and this I had borrowed; as if to say: That I have lost through the slackness of negligence, which I received from the grace of the Redeemer that I might render it through good works. But God never forsakes the mind that truly acknowledges itself in sins. Whence Eliseus cast the wood down and brought the iron to the surface, because the Redeemer humbles the sinner's heart and restores the understanding which it had lost. Whence in another translation it is said: that he broke the wood and threw it, and so raised the iron. To break the wood is to crush the heart from elation; to throw it down, to humble it by the thought of its own weakness. At once the iron returns, because the understanding runs back to the use of its former exercise.
15_interl1576: the understanding of the heart is lost through the slackness of negligence
15_interl1577: the spirit returned to the flesh
15_interl1578: Earthly power, minded proudly, persecutes the sons of light
15_interl1579: by the doctrine of our Lord the snares of the enemies are guarded against
15_marg1248: RABANUS. He who, trusting in the arms of wickedness, prepares snares for the servants of Christ, blinded by the night of perfidy, wages war against the Church.
15_marg1249: RABANUS. By these he notes those who through faintness of heart fear bodily punishments.
15_marg1250: "Fear ye not them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do to you."
15_marg1251: RABANUS. "I can ask my Father, and he will give me presently more than twelve legions of angels."
15_marg1252: LORD, OPEN THE EYES. RABANUS. It is very necessary that our Eliseus open the eyes of the heart to consider that all who trust in him shall not be confounded.
15_marg1253: STRIKE, I BESEECH THEE, THIS PEOPLE WITH BLINDNESS. RABANUS. It is good that the eye that scandalizes be plucked out, that the gaze of pride and malice may be stopped up, and the eye of sound faith and simplicity opened.
15_marg1254: RABANUS. After Eliseus led the enemies into Samaria, he did not permit them to be killed, but, preparing refreshment for them, sent them away in peace. And Saul, long kicking against the goad, the Lord first blinded, then enriched with spiritual knowledge. And he commanded us thus: "Love your enemies: do good to them that hate you."
15_marg1255: BENADAD GATHERED etc. RABANUS. Benadad and his army are the devil and the wicked, namely pagans, Jews, heretics, whom he stirs up to wage war against the Church. By such the people of God is afflicted which is set in Samaria, that is, in the keeping of the law. And there is famine when the teachers are not permitted to preach the word of God. But when Eliseus reveals it, that is, when the Redeemer shows through the gospel, the salvation which is far from sinners is known to be near to those who fear God. For the Lord says: "Tomorrow a bushel" etc. The bushel of fine flour is the perfect measure of divine wisdom, which is in the New Testament. "Two bushels of barley" are the knowledge of the law and the prophets, which are compared to one stater, that is, the catholic faith. "In the gate of Samaria," that is, in the apostolic preaching, through which one enters the Church. For when the storm of persecution which happens today ceases, the Lord will give tomorrow, that is, in the time to come, tranquillity, that preaching may be perfectly fulfilled.
15_marg1256: FOUR LEPROUS MEN. RABANUS. The lepers are those who, given to various vices or entangled in errors, bringing out foulness from an inward plague, show it on the skin. These the Lord often, converting them to faith and cleansing them from vices, makes messengers of true salvation. Whence Matthew from a publican [became] an apostle. And after the resurrection he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils; "she went and told them that had been with him, who were mourning." The lepers, entering the camp of the Syrians, were refreshed and carry off gold and silver, when the despised, giving their effort to the philosophy of this world, acquire both subtlety of sense and comeliness of speech, whence, well instructed, they can serve the uses of the Church. They are well said to be four, that, steeped in the teaching of the four gospels, they may preach the truth of the faith in the four parts of the world.
15_marg1257: AND THE KING [APPOINTED] THAT LORD etc. The lord holds the type of the scribes and Pharisees, to whom the Truth says: "Woe to you scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because you shut the kingdom of heaven against men, for you yourselves do not enter in; and those that are going in, you suffer not to enter." Whom the people trod upon in the gate, because he hindered the step of those entering into faith. Whence, deservedly trodden down, that is, condemned by the examination of the just judge, he will be cast into perpetual darkness.
15_interl1582: or in the sight of the Lord
15_marg1258: THOU SHALT SEE JEHU. RABANUS. Jehu designates the sovereignty of the gentiles, which the Lord destined to destroy with just vengeance the sacrilegious city that killed the prophets and the Lord of the prophets and persecuted his apostles, and to destroy the priesthood which it had held in vain after Christ, and overthrow the temple, and also to cast down from the height of the kingdom the impious Synagogue, which ever thirsted for the blood of the saints, and to kill its rulers.
15_marg1259: OCHOZIAS REIGNED OVER JUDA. RABANUS. It is said of Ochozias that he was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and reigned one year. For his father Joram is said to have reigned eight years and lived forty; if so, he is two years older than his father. But the Hebrews hand down that Joram lived forty years and reigned twenty-eight, of which eight are given to him, because so long he lived justly; the twenty in which he afterwards reigned in sickness and tribulation are added to his son, who was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and reigned one.
15_marg1260: RABANUS. Athalia, who strove to extinguish the seed of David, expresses the impiety of the Synagogue, which lay in wait for the seed of David, that is, Christ. She seemed for a time to reign, when she observed the ceremonies of the law temporally; for Athalia is interpreted 'temporal of the Lord'. But by the diligence of Josaba, who is interpreted 'fulness of the Lord', that is, of the Church, in which are true delights, Joas is kept, that is, 'memory of the Lord', namely Christ, in whom is the memory of the name of the Lord, lest he be destroyed in the hearts of the elect by the cruelty of the raging enemy. Rather he is nourished in the house of Joiada, which means 'beloved of the Lord', of whom the Father [says]: "This is my beloved Son." Whose house is holy Church, where, abiding in the holy faith of the elect, he daily makes increase of his body, until at the time of judgment he lifts up the sceptre of the kingdom and power against those who thought to bring him down, and has consigned the murderess of the saints to eternal punishments.
15_marg1261: AND IN THE SEVENTH YEAR etc. There were twenty-four courses of priests, Levites and porters, and they had as many high priests, who each succeeded one another in order through as many weeks, each having under him twenty-four priests and as many Levites, and porters of the same number. When, then, a new high priest entered on his office on the sabbath with a new band of priests, Levites and porters, the high priest who had ministered for the past week with his band returned home to his wife after the sabbath. For as long as they ministered they abstained from the conjugal act, remaining in the porches about the house of the Lord until the sabbath. But then the chief priest, because of the need of increasing the force, both kept back those who had completed the week and received those who were to fulfil it. He also gathered other Levites from the cities and the heads of families, whom, being about to bring out the king's son, he arranged in such a manner that those who had completed the sabbath stood armed about the king in the inner places of the court; those who had come for the sabbath guarded the king's house, that is, the palace, and the gate of the shieldbearers, by which one went down from the temple to the palace; the rest of the multitude guarded the outer gates of the courts against the fury of the queen, if she attempted anything. Afterwards he brought the king out of the house of the Lord, where he had been hidden, and they came by the way of the gate of the shieldbearers into the palace, and he sat upon the throne of the kings.
15_interl1586: that is, he made a compact with the chiefs of the Levites
15_marg1262: RABANUS. The gate of Sur and the house of Messa, which are named with the gate of the shieldbearers, seem to be in the palace.
15_interl1587: RABANUS. which is called the gate of the shieldbearers and the foundation
15_marg1263: RABANUS. The shieldbearers were the king's guards, keeping the vestibule of the palace.
15_interl1589: which David, having slain his enemies, consecrated in the house of the Lord, with which the Levites might be armed in war
15_marg1264: RABANUS. In the book of the Days more plainly: "And they put upon him the diadem, and gave into his hand the law to hold." And it was indeed of wholesome prudence that, after the slaying of the tyrannical queen, to the king's son succeeding to the kingdom the discipline of God's law should be committed to be kept together with the very dress of royalty, and that he who saw himself set over the people to rule them should remember that he himself ought to be subject to the divine laws to be ruled.
15_interl1591: the law of God, by which he may be taught how to live and what to do
15_marg1265: JOIADA MADE A COVENANT BETWEEN THE LORD AND THE KING etc. In Paralipomenon: "between himself," because he set himself in the place of the king and of God, whose minister he was. Whence Joiada is interpreted 'recognizing the Lord' or 'loving', because he taught to know and love the Lord.
15_marg1266: He made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that the king and the people should serve the Lord; he made [one] between the king and the people, that the people should deal faithfully toward the king, and the king rule the people with justice.
15_interl1593: Whence in Exodus: "When thou takest the sum of the children of Israel, every one of them shall give a price for their souls, and there shall be no scourge" for the price of a soul.
15_marg1267: AND JOAS SAID TO THE PRIESTS: ALL THE MONEY. Our king commands that the teachers receive all the money of spiritual knowledge or good examples which is brought by the just passing by into the treasury of the Lord, [and that it] be applied through the offices of the preachers to the restoring of the spiritual temple, so that they may repair there whatever they find torn by error or vices, lest perhaps the multitude of hearers perish through the negligence of the masters.
15_marg1268: RABANUS. He means the ruins of the house of the Lord, that what had begun to fall might be propped up. For it is read in Paralipomenon that Athalia and her sons, that is, the priests of the idols (because she is read not to have had a son), destroyed the house of the Lord and made Baal of the sanctified things.
15_marg1269: RABANUS. Before the coming of Christ, though the teaching of the law was in the Jewish nation, yet it was corrupted in many things through the negligence of the teachers, until he should come who gave the law and should teach that the decalogue in the writings of Moses and the prophets is to be observed spiritually through faith in the holy Trinity.
15_marg1270: RABANUS. The Lord says to the gospel teachers: "Preach the gospel to every creature," "heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers; freely have you received, freely give."
15_marg1271: RABANUS. Our high priest, who offered himself a victim to God, set one chest, that is, he made one catholic Church, for which he opened a hole above, because from it he prepared a passage to heaven.
15_marg1272: RABANUS. The altar is the body of the Lord, beside which is the chest, when the Church is joined to Christ, on the right hand of those entering the house. Because those who enter the Church through faith aim to come to eternal beatitude, which the right hand signifies. Thither, then, the priests who keep the doors of the temple put all the money that is brought to the temple, when the preachers who keep the entrance of faith offer the vows of the faithful in words and works and duly commend them to God with prayers in the Church.
15_marg1273: RABANUS. The chief ones are the teachers who gave the money collected, according to number and measure, to those who were over the carpenters and masons, that is, to the dispensers of the word of God, who gave the measure of gospel wheat to their fellow servants, to those who work in the house of the Lord and put together the works of the virtues in the divine building.
15_marg1274: RABANUS. The apostles, whom divine election set as princes in the Church, scattered the seeds of the word through the whole world by their disciples, so that they might set over their hearers workmen fit for the will of God; of whom some wrought wood, when they strove to prepare themselves and those obedient to them as fruitful trees in the house of the Lord; others made the repairs of the temple, when they rebuilt what had been broken by heresy and schisms; others cut stones, when they strongly rebuked the hard of heart and unbelieving; so that the restoration was fulfilled in all things that needed expense for strengthening the house of the Lord, according to that: "But to every one of us is given grace, according to the measure of the giving of Christ."
15_interl1595: containing the water of divine wisdom
15_marg1275: BUT YET THERE WERE NOT MADE etc. RABANUS. The method of forming vessels for the ministry of the Lord must be one thing, that of preparing wood and stones for the building of the house another; because the teaching by which the unlearned are steeped in faith must be one thing, and that by which those already perfect are instructed to the fulness of knowledge another. The vessels of the Lord are those who are already fit to receive the divine gifts and are apt for the ministry of God.
15_marg1276: There were not made of the same money water pots etc. In Paralipomenon: "And when they had finished all the work, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Joiada, and of it were made vessels for the temple." It is not contrary, because the vessels for the ministry of the temple were not made of the same money that was offered by the people for the repair of the house of the Lord, but of the remaining part of the money, which had been gathered also from other gifts.
15_marg1277: RABANUS. [The fleshhooks are] the teachers, whose office is to distribute the body and blood of the Lord to believers, to deny it to unbelievers, and also to apportion the spiritual food of the word to each as is fitting; because there are things in the words of God which he has deigned to reveal to our lowliness, [and] there are others which transcend the measure of our capacity.
15_marg1278: RABANUS. [The censers] are those who offer pure prayer to God from a pure conscience and faith unfeigned, and say: "Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight."
15_marg1279: RABANUS. [The trumpets are] the teachers who send forth through the whole world the voice of gospel preaching. Whence: "Lift up thy voice like a trumpet."
15_marg1280: RABANUS. They were so religious that no one doubted that they handled God's money without fraud. Whence it is clear how great discretion is needed by those who dispense to their fellow servants the money of the word of God, of which account must be rendered, that these may be found no less faithful in spiritual things than those in bodily.
15_interl1596: whence in Exodus: "When thou takest the sum of the children of Israel, every one of them shall give a price for their souls, and there shall be no scourge"
15_marg1281: RABANUS. Here it is shown that the confession of sins and penance is to be carried out not by each one's own judgment but by that of the priests, whose it is to discern between clean and unclean and to judge the spot of leprosy.
15_marg1282: NOW ELISEUS WAS SICK. RABANUS. Our Redeemer commands the rulers of the Church to put on spiritual arms and fight against the ancient enemy. The bow is the sacred word, which consists of both Testaments as of horn and string. The Old is the horn on account of its hardness, the New the string; and while the string is drawn the horn is bent, because when the New Testament is discussed the Old is bent from its rigour to spiritual understanding. The arrows are the words which the teachers bring forth. We, then, bend the bow when we weigh the sayings of sacred Scripture; we send forth arrows when we give words of doctrine.
15_marg1283: RABANUS. By his examples the Lord directs and strengthens the actions of teachers.
15_marg1284: OPEN THE WINDOW TO THE EAST etc. RABANUS. He exhorts his own first to be enlightened with the light of knowledge, and so to send the darts of words.
15_interl1598: that is, in holding or seizing
15_marg1285: THE ARROW OF DELIVERANCE etc. RABANUS. Holy preaching is the surest slaying of spiritual enemies if it is carried on perseveringly. Whence the teacher ought not through avarice to neglect the care of souls, but rather through piety to press on to the eternal rest which Aphec signifies; for it is interpreted 'will hold' or 'will seize'. Whence the Apostle, having enumerated the vices, added: "But thou, O man of God, fly these things: and pursue justice, godliness," lay hold on eternal life.
15_marg1286: AND WHEN HE HAD TAKEN THEM, HE SAID TO HIM AGAIN: STRIKE etc. RABANUS. The teachers are commanded to strike the earth, that is, the carnal, with the dart of preaching. To strike the earth three times with the dart is to instil the faith of the Trinity into the carnal by teaching. Afterwards let them be taught to command the five bodily senses and to spend their zeal on good works, which are expressed by six, and also to meditate earnestly on the spiritual knowledge which the sevenfold Spirit put forth in the twin Testament for the salvation of the human race. But those who believe that faith alone suffices for salvation are rightly reproved, because, according to James: "Faith without works is dead."
15_marg1287: RABANUS. The rising of the body through touching the bones of Eliseus signifies that whoever with firm faith touches the death of Christ and truly places his hope in him will without doubt be a partaker of his resurrection. Whence: "I am the resurrection and the life."
15_marg1288: "After the death of Joiada, the princes of Juda went in, and worshipped the king" etc. The Jews say that the king was worshipped as God and gladly accepted from his subjects honours beyond human measure. Whence he suddenly experienced the wrath of God, like Herod.
15_marg1289: There is no God in Israel, because all were guilty and polluted with idolatry. See that these two glosses are taken over from the twenty-fourth <chapter> of Second Paralipomenon, and have their place there rather than here.
15_marg1290: RABANUS. Amasias did good in the sight of the Lord, but not with a perfect heart. For he did the good works which please God, but not with a perfect heart, because he showed them under a feigned appearance before men, and so they were not acceptable before God.
15_interl1601: the old edition put 'Gemela' as if the name of a region
15_marg1291: RABANUS. The valley of the Saltpits was where they made salt: either from salt hay cut, dried and burnt; or from the salt waters of wells boiled and brought by cooking to the firmness of salt; or by any other method by which salt is wont to be made.
15_marg1292: RABANUS. Petra is a noble city of Arabia in the land of Edom, which in the book of Numbers is called Recem, and is so named by the Syrians. But Josephus calls it not a city but a great rock set in Arabia.
15_marg1293: [Jectehel,] the name Amasias as victor gave it, is interpreted 'assembly of God' or 'help of God', he acting faithfully, that it might seem of everlasting memory that either the assembly of the people of God, or he with God's help, took it.
15_marg1294: HE RESTORED THE BORDERS OF ISRAEL FROM THE ENTRANCE. RABANUS. It is said of Jeroboam: He restored the borders of Israel from the entrance of Emath unto the sea of the wilderness. Emath, which is now called Epiphania, was the northern border of Israel. And the sea of the wilderness is the Dead Sea, which extends in breadth five hundred and eighty stadia as far as Zoara of Arabia, in length one hundred and fifty as far as the neighbourhood of Sodom. Jeroboam, then, encamping against the Syrians, laid waste all their province, as Jonas had prophesied.
15_marg1295: Ophel was a tower not far from the temple, of enormous size and height. Whence it is called Ophel, that is, 'of darkness' or 'of the clouds', because it lifts its head to the clouds; which in Zacharias is called 'the cloudy tower'.
15_marg1296: RABANUS. He is Ozias, who, when he wished to sacrifice in the temple against the law of Moses, was struck with leprosy. He signifies the devil, to whom the leprosy of iniquity is incurable; who, when he sought things greater than himself, being made notable by the foulness of the worst leprosy, was cast out of the house, and remains a leper to the end, separated from the people of God. While he reigned, Isaias the prophet did not lift his eyes to heaven; the heavenly things were not unbarred to him, except after he died. While Pharao lived, the people of Israel did not sigh to God out of the work of clay and straw; but after Pharao's death their cry went up to the Lord. If, then, you understand contrary powers in Ozias and Pharao, you will see how, while they live, none of ours sees and sighs. While sin reigns, we build cities for the Egyptians, we are busied in filth. Ozias built the gate of the valley, which above is called the gate of Ephraim.
15_marg1297: HE BUILT. RABANUS. Joatham built the high gate of the house of the Lord, which in the Acts of the Apostles is called the Beautiful, and by the Hebrews is called 'the gate of Joatham'.
15_interl1606: in the valley of Beennom; this is the valley of the son of Ennom
15_marg1298: RABANUS. Beennom, 'of the son of Ennom'. Topheth or Thaphet is in the valley of Beennom near Haceldama, a place once most pleasant, where they used to sacrifice to demons. In Hebrew Gehennom, that is, 'valley of Ennom', whence in the gospel it is called 'gehenna'; because as those who worshipped idols perished there in body and soul, so sinners who pass to hell will be punished with eternal damnation.
15_interl1607: not for the sake of religion but of light
15_marg1299: THE MUSACH OF THE SABBATH. RABANUS. It is a building placed in the vestibule of the temple, where kings, when they went to the temple on the sabbath, put in alms. And so the Musach of the sabbath is the treasury of the kings, as the corbona is of the priests.
15_marg1300: MUSACH etc. AND THE KING'S ENTRY FROM WITHOUT. RABANUS. He did not turn it into the temple of the Lord in order that it might serve the worship of God in it, but that it might be profaned with the temple, he being eager to please the king of the Assyrians rather than God, so that when he came there, seeing it, he might covet it and carry it off, as many other things, Achaz giving them to him, by which he might find his favour.
15_interl1609: that is, from the fort to the city
15_interl1610: He warned thus, as in the second to Timothy: "I charge thee, before God."
15_interl1614: or the kingdom of Juda, as Benjamin and Levi too were commonly called
15_marg1301: AND THE KING OF THE ASSYRIANS BROUGHT. RABANUS. The Assyrian king, that is, the devil, with his army daily afflicts the ecclesiastical people by besieging and laying it waste, when, tearing them from their own seats for sins committed, he carries them into a strange land. Whence: "Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: when we remembered Sion."
15_marg1302: AND EVERY NATION MADE. RABANUS. In the book of places it is read that Benoth and Nerguel were cities which those who had passed over from Babylonia built in Judea. Asuna too was a town built by those who had come to it from Emath. Nebaam and Tharcha are cities which the Hevites founded in Judea.
15_marg1303: RABANUS. It seems, according to the sequence of the discourse, that the names here can also be understood of the idols which these nations had formerly served; because when it had been said, And every nation made gods of their own, it is added as if to complete the sentence: For the men of Babylon made Socoth Benoth, that is, the tabernacles of Benoth, which is the name of an idol. In what follows Adramelech and Anamelech are shown to have been idols of the city of Sepharvaim. So it seems to follow that Nergel of the Cutheans, Asuna of the Emathites, Nebaath and Tharcha were idols of the Hevites.
15_marg1304: The heretics have certain sacraments in common with holy Church, and understand rightly certain sentences of the Scriptures, but yet they serve the idols of unclean spirits. It seems to them that they rightly keep the fear of God when they think they favour the truth according to their own sense. But because they spurn the unity of the catholic faith, they obey the wills of evil spirits. And not only the first inventors of errors, whom the fathers of the Samaritans signify, do this, but also their followers, whom we understand by the name of sons and grandsons.
